AXP.rationale: American Express shows solid fundamental health with consistent revenue and EPS growth (Q1 2026 revenue +9.3% YoY, EPS +17.6% YoY), strong profitability (ROE 33%, net margin 26.6%), and a durable closed-loop business model. The company reaffirmed 2026 guidance for 9-10% revenue growth and EPS of $17.30-$17.90. Valuation is attractive vs its own history: current P/E of 19.1x sits at the low end of its 18.4-25.3x 365-day range, and P/B of 6.3x is near the bottom of its 6.1-8.2x range, having compressed from 8.0x in Dec 2025. The stock is down ~16% from its 52-week high of $387.49, creating a meaningful discount. Credit quality remains healthy with a 2% net write-off rate and 1.4% delinquency rate. However, risks include rising 10-year Treasury yields (4.47%, up 8.5% over 90 days), elevated oil prices ($96.83), and competitive pressure from Capital One/Discover merger and JPMorgan's Sapphire Reserve. Operating cash flow declined 20% YoY in Q1, and the balance sheet shows rising leverage (debt-to-equity 1.73x). Near-term catalysts are limited — no major earnings event or regulatory catalyst imminent — though the Fanatics partnership and 16% dividend increase provide modest support. The score reflects a quality franchise at a reasonable valuation with manageable but real macro headwinds.
